description_full: PT Bukit Asam (Persero) Tbk, together with its subsidiaries, engages in coal mining activities in Indonesia. The company's coal mining activities include general surveying, exploration, exploitation, processing, refining, transportation, and trading. It maintains special coal dock facilities; operates steam-fired power plants; and engages in the mining of coal methane gas. The company also offers briquette processing, mining services, palm plantation and processing, and health services, as well as real estate and construction services. In addition, it engages in the hospital clinic and polyclinic; rental; port; and trade, services, workshop, development, industry, and transportation businesses. It also exports its products to India, South Korea, China, Cambodia, Vietnam, Japan, Bangladesh, Thailand, Taiwan, Philippines, Malaysia, Hong Kong, Spain, and Romania. The company was formerly known as PT Bukit Asam Tbk and was changed to PT Bukit Asam (Persero) Tbk in February 2026. PT Bukit Asam (Persero) Tbk was founded in 1876 and is headquartered in Tanjung Enim Selatan, Indonesia. PT Bukit Asam (Persero) Tbk operates as a subsidiary of PT Mineral Industri Indonesia (Persero).

financial_summary: PT Bukit Asam Persero TBK is a small-cap energy business with a $2.0B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are contracting by -9.1pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.

Returns on capital run at 28% against a 8% cost of capital — a 20-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 21% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $152M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.
Management returns a meaningful 10.7% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation.
